recipes.name: Home-Style Chicken Curry
method: Heat oil and fry cumin seeds until they crackle.
Add onion and cook on medium for 10 minutes until deep golden.
Add garlic and ginger, cook 1 minute, then turmeric, chilli and ground coriander for 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes and cook until they break down and oil separates, about 8 minutes.
Add chicken, stir to coat, then stir in yoghurt a spoonful at a time.
Cover and simmer 20–25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in garam masala, season, and finish with coriander. Serve with rice.
recipes.notes: Freezes well for up to 3 months. Flavour improves the next day.

recipes.name: Butter Chicken (Lighter)
method: Mix chicken with yoghurt, half the garam masala, chilli and salt. Marinate at least 30 minutes.
Grill or pan-sear the chicken until charred at the edges. Set aside.
Melt butter, cook onion 8 minutes, then garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add cumin and remaining garam masala, then tomatoes. Simmer 10 minutes and blend smooth.
Return chicken to the sauce, stir in cream and crushed fenugreek, simmer 5 minutes.
Season and serve with rice.
recipes.notes: Uses light cream and less butter than restaurant versions.

recipes.name: Chicken Biryani

ingredients.name: Whole spices (cardamom, cloves, bay leaf, cinnamon)

method: Marinate chicken with yoghurt, garlic, ginger, turmeric, chilli, masala and salt for 1 hour.
Fry onions in oil until deep brown and crisp. Remove half for garnish.
Add marinated chicken and tomatoes to the pot and cook 15 minutes until mostly cooked.
Meanwhile, boil rice with whole spices and salt for 5–6 minutes until 70% cooked. Drain.
Layer rice over the chicken. Scatter mint, coriander, fried onions and saffron milk.
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 25 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes, then gently mix from the bottom when serving.
recipes.notes: Freeze in portions; reheat with a splash of water to steam.

recipes.name: Oven Tandoori Chicken
method: Mix yoghurt, lemon juice, garlic, ginger, spices, oil and salt.
Coat chicken and marinate at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Heat oven to 220°C. Arrange chicken on a rack over a lined tray.
Bake 30–35 minutes, turning once, until charred and cooked through.
Serve with sliced red onion, lemon wedges and salad.
recipes.notes: Marinated raw chicken freezes well. Defrost in the fridge before baking.

recipes.name: Kerala Fish Curry
method: Soak kokum in a little warm water for 10 minutes.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds and curry leaves, then onion, garlic, ginger and chillies. Cook 6 minutes.
Add spices and cook 30 seconds, then tomatoes until soft.
Add kokum with its water and about 200 ml water. Simmer 5 minutes.
Slide in the fish and simmer gently 6–8 minutes without stirring too much.
Stir in coconut milk, warm through without boiling, and season. Serve with rice.
recipes.notes: Uses kokum for the classic sour note. Fish texture suffers when frozen, so eat within 2 days.

recipes.name: Tadka Dal
method: Boil lentils with turmeric and 900 ml water for 20 minutes until soft. Whisk smooth.
In a separate pan, heat ghee and fry cumin and mustard seeds until they pop.
Add onion and cook until golden, then garlic, ginger, chilli and chilli powder.
Add tomatoes and cook until soft, then pour this tadka into the dal.
Simmer 5 minutes, adjust thickness with water, season and garnish with coriander.
recipes.notes: Add a handful of spinach at the end for extra greens.

recipes.name: Sambar
method: Pressure-cook or boil toor dal with turmeric until completely soft. Mash.
Boil vegetables, onion and tomato in 600 ml water until just tender.
Add tamarind, sambar powder and salt. Simmer 8 minutes.
Stir in the dal and simmer another 5 minutes.
Temper: fry mustard seeds, dried chillies, asafoetida and curry leaves in oil. Pour over the sambar.
Garnish with coriander. Serve with rice, idli or dosa.

recipes.name: Tomato Pepper Rasam
method: Simmer tomatoes, tamarind, garlic, pepper, cumin, turmeric and salt in 800 ml water for 10 minutes.
Lightly mash the tomatoes and simmer until frothy on top. Do not boil hard.
Temper mustard seeds, asafoetida and curry leaves in ghee and pour over.
Add coriander. Drink as a soup or serve over rice.
recipes.notes: Light and soothing. Pairs with a protein dish rather than being a meal on its own.

recipes.name: Pork Vindaloo
method: Blend soaked chillies, garlic, ginger, whole spices, turmeric, vinegar and sugar into a paste.
Coat pork in half the paste and marinate at least 2 hours, ideally overnight.
Brown onions in oil, add remaining paste and fry 3 minutes.
Add pork and brown lightly, then add 300 ml water.
Cover and simmer 75–90 minutes until tender, adding water if needed.
Season. Rest overnight if you can for the best flavour.
recipes.notes: Goan-style: tangy and hot. Freezes very well.

recipes.name: Egg Curry
method: Lightly score the boiled eggs and fry in a little oil with turmeric until blistered. Set aside.
Cook onion until golden, then garlic and ginger.
Add spices for 30 seconds, then tomatoes. Cook until jammy.
Add 200 ml water (and coconut milk if using) and simmer 8 minutes.
Add eggs, simmer 5 minutes, finish with garam masala and coriander.
recipes.notes: Boiled eggs go rubbery when frozen. Keep leftovers in the fridge for up to 2 days.

recipes.name: Chana Masala
method: Fry cumin seeds in oil, then onion until deep golden.
Add garlic, ginger and chilli, then turmeric and masala.
Add tomatoes and cook until thick and the oil separates.
Add chickpeas and 250 ml water. Simmer 15 minutes, mashing a few to thicken.
Finish with amchur and coriander. Serve with rice or roti.

recipes.name: Keema Matar
method: Fry cumin seeds, then onion until golden.
Add garlic, ginger and spices, then the mince. Break it up and brown well.
Add tomatoes and cook 10 minutes until the mixture is dry-ish.
Add peas and 100 ml water, cover and cook 8 minutes.
Finish with garam masala and coriander. Serve with rice or roti.
recipes.notes: Also great stuffed into toasted wraps. Freezes well.

recipes.name: Mulligatawny Soup
method: Soften onion, carrot, garlic and ginger in oil for 8 minutes.
Add curry powder and turmeric for 30 seconds, then the lentils, apple and stock.
Add chicken thighs whole and simmer 30 minutes.
Remove chicken and shred. Blend the soup until mostly smooth.
Return chicken, add coconut milk, season, and serve over a spoon of rice with lemon.

recipes.name: Railway Lamb Curry
method: Brown lamb in batches in oil. Set aside.
Fry whole spices and onions until golden, then garlic and ginger.
Add curry and chilli powder, then tomatoes. Cook 5 minutes.
Return lamb with 500 ml water. Cover and simmer 60 minutes.
Add potatoes and tamarind. Simmer 25 minutes more until tender.
Stir in coconut milk if using, season and serve.
recipes.notes: The classic dining-car curry: mild, tangy and made to keep.

recipes.name: Devil Chicken Curry
method: Fry onion until soft, then garlic, ginger and capsicum for 3 minutes.
Add chicken with turmeric and chilli. Cook on high until lightly browned.
Stir in vinegar, tomato sauce, soy and mustard with 100 ml water.
Simmer uncovered 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the sauce is glossy.
Season. Serve with rice or crusty bread.
recipes.notes: Traditionally a Boxing Day dish for leftover roast. Swap in cooked chicken and cut simmering to 5 minutes.

recipes.name: Kedgeree
method: Poach the fish in 600 ml water for 6 minutes. Lift out and flake, keeping the water.
Soften onion in butter, add curry powder and turmeric, then the rice.
Add the fish water, cover and cook 12 minutes. Stir in peas for the last 3.
Fold through the flaked fish and lemon juice. Season.
Top with eggs and herbs.

recipes.name: Ball Curry (Kofta Curry)
method: Mix mince with egg, half an onion (grated), half the garlic and ginger, chilli, garam masala, salt and coriander.
Roll into walnut-size balls. Chill 15 minutes.
Fry remaining onion until golden, then garlic, ginger, curry powder and turmeric.
Add tomatoes and cook until thick, then 200 ml water.
Drop in the balls and simmer covered 20 minutes without stirring. Shake the pan gently.
Add coconut milk and simmer 5 minutes more. Season and serve.
recipes.notes: Freeze cooked balls in the sauce.

recipes.name: Country Captain Chicken
method: Season chicken with salt, pepper and half the curry powder. Brown well and set aside.
Fry onion, garlic and capsicum until soft.
Add remaining curry powder and turmeric, then tomatoes and sultanas.
Return chicken, cover and simmer 25 minutes.
Scatter with almonds and serve with rice.

recipes.name: Roast Chicken & Vegetables

ingredients.name: Roast chicken rub or dried herbs

method: Heat oven to 200°C. Pat chicken dry and rub with oil, salt and the rub.
Stuff the cavity with halved lemon and a few garlic cloves.
Toss vegetables with oil and salt around the chicken in a large tray.
Roast 70–80 minutes until juices run clear (75°C in the thigh).
Rest 10 minutes before carving. Steam greens while it rests.
recipes.notes: Strip leftover meat for Devil Chicken Curry, sandwiches or soup. Freeze the carcass for stock.

recipes.name: Beef & Vegetable Casserole
method: Heat oven to 160°C. Toss beef in seasoned flour and brown in batches in a casserole dish.
Soften onion, carrot and celery in the same dish.
Return beef with mushrooms, tomatoes, stock, Worcestershire and bay leaves.
Cover and bake 2–2½ hours until the beef is tender.
Season and serve with mash or crusty bread.
recipes.notes: Slow cooker: 8 hours on low. Freezes very well.

recipes.name: Grilled Barramundi with Greens
method: Pat fish very dry, season and score the skin.
Cook skin-side down in a hot oiled pan for 5 minutes, pressing flat, until crisp.
Flip and cook 2–3 minutes more. Squeeze over lemon.
Meanwhile stir-fry garlic, broccolini and bok choy with a splash of water for 3 minutes.
Serve fish on the greens with lemon wedges.
recipes.notes: Weeknight-fast. Also works with snapper or salmon.

recipes.name: Chicken & Bok Choy Stir Fry
method: Toss chicken with 1 tbsp soy and the cornflour.
Stir-fry chicken in a very hot wok in two batches until just cooked. Set aside.
Stir-fry garlic, ginger and mushrooms for 2 minutes, then bok choy stems.
Add bok choy leaves, chicken, remaining soy, oyster sauce and a splash of water.
Toss 1 minute, add spring onion, and serve with rice.
recipes.notes: Frozen bok choy portions from your freezer work fine; add straight from frozen.

recipes.name: Beef & Chinese Broccoli Stir Fry
method: Toss beef with soy and cornflour.
Sear beef in a smoking-hot wok in batches, 1 minute each. Set aside.
Stir-fry onion and garlic 2 minutes, add gai lan stems, then leaves with a splash of water.
Return beef with oyster sauce and toss 1 minute.
Serve immediately with rice.

recipes.name: Pumpkin Soup
method: Soften onion and garlic in oil for 5 minutes.
Add pumpkin, potato and stock. Simmer 20 minutes until very soft.
Blend until smooth. Add nutmeg and season.
Swirl through cream to serve.
recipes.notes: Low in protein on its own. Serve with a protein side or stir through shredded chicken.

recipes.name: Spaghetti Bolognese
method: Soften onion, carrot, celery and garlic in oil for 8 minutes.
Add mince and brown well, breaking it up.
Stir in tomato paste, then tomatoes, herbs and 200 ml water.
Simmer gently 45 minutes, partly covered. Season.
Cook spaghetti and serve with the sauce and parmesan.
recipes.notes: Freeze the sauce on its own (not with the pasta).

recipes.name: Creamy Chicken & Mushroom Pasta (Light)
method: Cook pasta, keeping a cup of the water.
Brown chicken in oil, season, and set aside.
Fry mushrooms until golden, then garlic for 30 seconds.
Add cream and parmesan, simmer 2 minutes, then add spinach until wilted.
Toss through pasta and chicken, loosening with pasta water.

recipes.name: Chicken & Vegetable Soup
method: Soften onion, carrot, celery and garlic in oil for 8 minutes.
Add stock, bay leaves and whole chicken thighs. Simmer 25 minutes.
Remove chicken, shred, and return to the pot.
Add zucchini and pasta. Simmer 10 minutes. Season.
recipes.notes: Freeze without the pasta for the best texture.

recipes.name: Cottage Pie
method: Boil potatoes until tender, then mash with milk and seasoning.
Brown mince with onion and carrot.
Stir in tomato paste, Worcestershire and stock. Simmer 20 minutes until thick. Add peas.
Spread mince in a baking dish, top with mash and cheese.
Bake at 200°C for 25 minutes until golden.
recipes.notes: Assemble and freeze unbaked. Bake from thawed.

recipes.name: Chilli con Carne
method: Soften onion, garlic and capsicum in oil.
Add mince and brown well, then the spices for 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and 150 ml water. Simmer 30 minutes.
Stir in beans and simmer 10 minutes more. Season.
Serve with rice, a dollop of Greek yoghurt and coriander.
recipes.notes: Freezes very well in portions.

recipes.name: Spinach & Mushroom Omelette
method: Fry mushrooms in oil until golden. Add spinach until just wilted. Set aside.
Beat eggs with salt and pepper and pour into the hot pan.
Stir gently, then let set. Add the filling and cheese to one half.
Fold and slide onto a plate.
